geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

peak.note: 17 stacks up at Los Gatos from mid-afternoon
weekend beach traffic northbound in the evening
101 south through Sunnyvale is stop-and-go from 4
101 north is the worst of the peninsula — 280 is usually faster
101 north clogs from Redwood City at 3:30; the 280 split at Daly City is the second squeeze
weekend midday backs up into the city
the Caldecott is the pinch — eastbound clears by 7
Waldo Grade northbound is the bottleneck
Dumbarton eastbound is fine; the toll and the queue are on the way home
local arterials get slow around the school and commute peak

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: The Mountain Goats — Night Two: Alpha
events.note: Night two of a six-night Fillmore residency, each evening built on a different seam of the catalogue; tonight is the Alpha songs, the divorce-album cycle that runs through the early tape years. The venue publishes no door times.

events.title: Manic Street Preachers
events.note: Welsh agit-pop that has outlived every scene it was filed under — thirty-odd years of big choruses with reading lists attached. A 1,400-cap room is small for them.

events.title: Jorja Smith with Wesley Joseph
events.note: Walsall soul with a jazz singer's patience about where the beat sits. Sold out, and the Castro's balcony is the place to hear it.

events.title: Margaret Glaspy with Anna Tivel
events.note: Glaspy writes spare, slightly abrasive guitar songs and sings them like she is arguing with herself. Tivel opens with Portland story-songs. Doors seven, $24–28.

events.title: Finish Ticket (Final Show), Picture Atlantic, Field Medic
events.note: An East Bay band's last ever show, on a bill of Bay Area lifers, in a club that itself closes at the end of the year. Sold out. Doors seven, $20.

events.title: Krazy for Karaoke
events.note: The Knockout's Monday karaoke, which is less a singalong than a floor show. Read off the venue's DICE calendar.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Fifteen-plus years of all-vinyl Motown and Northern soul on a Monday. Free before eight, five dollars after, and the floor fills either way.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Nine to ten on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays the 1894 garden is free to all; city residents are free any time with ID. Go before the tour buses.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an RSVP, twenty-plus at the door without one. Standing weeknight room, useful mainly because it costs nothing.

events.title: Mirthquake: Monday Live Comedy in the Richmond
events.note: Free-ticketed stand-up in the avenues with $5 drinks, 21+. Lower-confidence listing: Funcheap names no room.

events.title: Los Telez
events.note: Cumbia and norteño covers for a dancing crowd. Found only on the regional sweep, so the time is unconfirmed.

events.title: Max Bien Kahn, Levi Thomas, Chelsea Blake
events.note: Three songwriters in a record shop — the kind of bill that exists because the room is small enough to allow it. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: Comeback Kid with Defeater and Dead Heat
events.note: Winnipeg hardcore with two decades of gang vocals behind it, plus Boston's Defeater and Oxnard's Dead Heat. Cornerstone's own calendar would not load; time unconfirmed.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night with HellaFunny
events.note: Temescal's standing Monday stand-up night, free with an RSVP.

events.title: Son Volt with Kelly Willis
events.note: Jay Farrar's thirty-year argument that Uncle Tupelo's harder half was the right half, with Texas country singer Kelly Willis along. Doors seven. Four minutes from Caltrain.

events.title: BOYNEXTDOOR: KNOCK ON Vol.2
events.note: Fourth-generation K-pop boy band on their second North American run, in a 2,300-cap theatre rather than an arena — which is the reason to go.

events.title: Son Volt with Kelly Willis
events.note: The second of two Bay Area nights, after Menlo Park on Monday. August Hall lists no door time.

events.title: Armored Saint and Metal Church with Livekill
events.note: Two first-wave American metal bands co-headlining — Armored Saint still fronted by John Bush, Metal Church playing the speed-metal canon. Doors six, $35–40.

events.title: Straight No Chaser
events.note: Ten-man a cappella, mostly holiday repertoire by this point in the year. Findable without help; listed for completeness.

events.title: Silverada with Emily Nenni
events.note: Austin honky-tonk (formerly Mike and the Moonpies) with Nashville's Emily Nenni, who sings harder country than most people signed to sing it.

events.title: Brokencyde, Dot Dot Curve, 9aradox
events.note: Crunkcore, revived without irony, for an audience that was fourteen in 2008. Doors 7:30, $28.

events.title: Soft Vein with Still Ruins and Blood Rave
events.note: Darkwave and industrial on a three-band local bill. Reached only through DNA's mirrors, which carry the touring concerts and none of the club nights.

events.title: Jammy Buffet
events.note: An evening of Phish-by-way-of-Margaritaville, which is either the best or the worst idea of the week. Doors seven, 21+.

events.title: Send for Help, Tuberose, Get Lost Cassidy Frost
events.note: Local punk and noise-pop three deep in a room that holds a hundred and fifty. From the venue's DICE calendar.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: The Mission's Tuesday karaoke, off Kilowatt's DICE calendar.

events.title: Counsellor at Law
events.note: William Wyler's 1933 courtroom picture in the Roxie's Wild, Weird, Wicked series of pre-Code films — John Barrymore as a Lower East Side lawyer who made good.

events.title: Neel: Seminars on Sonic Design — Sound as Shape
events.note: The Italian techno producer on how sound occupies space, presented with Recombinant. Gray Area publishes no start time for it.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: Drawing from a live model in a bar, materials on the table, no instruction. A standing Tuesday; no time published.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: The nightly free-with-RSVP room in Hayes Valley.

events.title: Thundercat: Distracted AF Tour, with Fera
events.note: Stephen Bruner's six-string bass sits exactly between Shuggie Otis and Flying Lotus, and live he plays more of it than the records let on. Doors seven. Take BART — downtown garages shut their gates at seven on weeknights.

events.title: Brian Culbertson
events.note: First of three nights of smooth jazz keyboard, sold out across the run. $89–139.

events.title: The Underachievers with Dizzy Wright
events.note: Brooklyn's psychedelic-leaning rap duo with Las Vegas's Dizzy Wright. Cornerstone's calendar did not load this run; found on the sweep.

events.title: Shark in the Water, Sharing the Road, Pied Piper KJ
events.note: Three local bands in the Ivy Room's narrow back half. Reached through JamBase, which gives no times — ivyroom.com fetches empty.

events.title: Las Migas
events.note: Barcelona's all-woman flamenco quartet, who put Catalan song and Mediterranean strings into the form without sanding its edges. A seated listening room suits them.

events.title: Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.note: Temescal's Tuesday stand-up, free with an RSVP.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: The standing Tuesday double bill at one of the last drive-ins in the region. Six dollars adults, two for children.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Calgary Flames
events.note: A Tuesday against Calgary, which keeps the upper bowl cheap. Diridon is ten minutes' walk and the only sane way in.

events.title: The Who's Tommy
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Opening night of the touring revival of the 1993 Broadway staging — Des McAnuff's production, rebuilt with projection instead of scaffolding. Six nights here.

events.title: Toast: The Best of Bread
events.note: A tribute to David Gates's soft-rock catalogue. The brief includes tribute acts and never features them; this is why.

events.title: Filoli Unwrapped
events.note: An hour behind the holiday decoration of the house, before the public rooms open. Also the 19th and the 22nd.

events.title: Goddamn Gallows with King Sickabilly
events.note: Gutter-punk bluegrass with a washboard and a banjo played like a weapon. Clears the drive only if this is already your thing — said plainly rather than talked up.

events.title: The Mountain Goats — Night Three: Stump the Band
events.note: The requests night of the residency: the audience names songs and the band finds out whether it remembers them. For a catalogue this deep that is a genuine event.

events.title: Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam: The Joint Tour
events.note: The Walkmen's singer and Vampire Weekend's former arranger, nearly a decade on from the record they made together. Leithauser's voice is the draw and the Castro's room is kind to it.

events.title: Icona Pop with Sorana
events.note: Swedish electropop still trading on one enormous 2012 single, playing a 500-cap club rather than a festival slot.

events.title: Jamila Woods: 10 Years of HEAVN, with Hannah Mayree
events.note: Chicago poet-singer playing her first record whole at ten years' remove — gospel harmony, Chicago house underneath, politics in plain speech. Moved here from August Hall, so the room is now half the size. Doors seven, $35–40.

events.title: Sueco with Jeris Johnson and Port London
events.note: Post-SoundCloud pop-punk with trap bones. Doors seven, $20–30.

events.title: John Carroll Kirby with Danny Paul Grody Duo
events.note: Session keyboardist turned new-age-adjacent bandleader — library-music textures played by people who can actually solo. Grody's guitar duo opens, which is the right pairing. Doors seven, $30–45.

events.title: Ninajirachi with MGNA Crrrta
events.note: Australian hyperpop-adjacent club producer. Lower confidence: the Regency publishes no dates of its own and the mirrors disagree about which nights this week she plays.

events.title: April Magazine, Black Thumb, The Babygirls
events.note: San Francisco's own hazy, slow-moving guitar pop, three bands of it. From the venue's DICE calendar.

events.title: Lapses, Half Rotten Goddes, E.F. Luka
events.note: Local bill in the Mission, read off Kilowatt's DICE calendar.

events.title: LAYA with DJ Trauma
events.note: Filipina-American R&B with a light touch on the production. Sold out — waitlist only.

events.title: Ken Russell's The Devils (4K restoration)
events.note: Russell's 1971 convent-hysteria film, long cut about and now restored. Also played Monday at eight; this is the second of two.

events.title: Staff Pick: Chicago, with drag show
events.note: Zann Nolan introduces the 2002 musical and then stages a drag show after it, which is the correct response to that film.

events.title: Free Admission Day at YBCA
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday — Dread Scott's The Body Politic and GaHee Park's Behind the Curtain are both up. Eleven till eight.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Velveteen Rabbit Pop-up Book
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two till four in the Grand Lobby, all ages, free with registration.

events.title: Progressive Art Studio Models: a lecture by Cléa Massiani
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: On studio models for disabled artists, in the Front Door Gallery. Free.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven — Ideas of Utopia in the BAMPFA Collection
events.note: A lunchtime walk through BAMPFA's utopia show with a docent. Free with admission.

events.title: Black Hole Collective Film Lab
events.note: Hand-processed and photochemical work from the Oakland film lab — 16mm as a craft rather than a format.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The free hour, nine to ten. Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

events.title: Biblio Bistro Farmers' Market Cooking School
events.note: Open-air cooking demonstration built from what is on the market stalls that morning. Free.

events.title: SF State Free Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: The university opens its roof and its telescopes, 6:30 to 8:30, free, weather permitting — which in November it may not be.

events.title: '80s NYC Underground: Mondo New York
events.note: The 1988 downtown-performance documentary, free, in a North Beach storefront gallery. Karen Finley, Joey Arias, Lydia Lunch.

events.title: Free Astronomy Talk: Chile's Giant Observatories
events.note: On the Atacama telescopes, free, seven till half eight on Corona Heights.

events.title: Astronomy on Tap SF
events.note: Working astronomers giving short talks in a nightclub, free with a one-drink minimum. Reliably the best value on a Wednesday.

events.title: 40th Annual Building Lighting and Holiday Market
events.note: Four till six: the downtown tower lighting with a market round it. Downtown SF names no address, so the location is lower-confidence.

events.title: Clue: Live On Stage
events.note: The stage version of the 1985 film, which keeps the three endings. Listed at seven on the resale feed; San Jose Stage publishes no schedule of its own.

events.title: The Who's Tommy
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Second of six performances.

events.title: Alice Cooper
events.note: Still touring the guillotine at seventy-eight, and the band is better than the spectacle needs it to be. $52 up.

events.title: Three Days Grace with I Prevail and The Funeral Portrait
events.note: Canadian post-grunge on a double bill with I Prevail. An arena show, findable without help; listed for completeness.

events.title: Leanna Firestone with Sydney Sprague
events.note: Internet-grown confessional pop that works better in a 500-cap room than the streaming numbers suggest. Doors six.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: The club's midweek showcase of whoever is passing through. $23.

events.title: Gianmarco Soresi
events.note: First of a ten-show, five-night run — the New York comic whose crowd work travels better than his specials. Second show 9:45. On a wait list.

events.title: Rachel Willis-Sørensen Vocal Recital
events.note: The American soprano in recital rather than in costume — a Bing Hall booking that would be a main-stage night anywhere else.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.note: San Francisco Opera's Figaro, in a run to 29 November. The Wednesday has the best remaining availability of the week. From $30.

events.title: Jim Brickman: Piano Sensation and a Little Bit of Christmas
events.note: Adult-contemporary piano with the holiday repertoire creeping in. The Fox publishes no time.

events.title: As I Lay Dying with The Curse Within
events.note: Metalcore with a complicated history. Does not clear the drive from Mountain View; noted because the band also plays Berkeley on Thursday.

events.title: Michael Nau
events.note: Cotton Jones's songwriter, playing the smallest room on his run. Found on the sweep.

events.title: The Mountain Goats — Night Four: The Sunset Tree
events.note: The Sunset Tree played whole — the 2005 record about surviving a stepfather, and the one most of the room came for. The night of the six to pick if you pick one.

events.title: RØZ: Se Está Haciendo Tarde
events.note: Mexican alt-pop on the Monster Energy Outbreak run — a Spanish-language booking in a 2,300-cap room, which the city gets less often than it should.

events.title: Pretty Sick with Sex Week
events.note: Sabrina Fuentes's band, grunge bones with a bass player's sense of where the hook lives.

events.title: Ruby Ibarra with The Balikbayans, Carl Angelo, Amihan
events.note: Filipina-American rapper from the South Bay who writes in English and Tagalog and whose live band gives the records teeth. A hometown bill four deep. Doors 7:30, $25 advance.

events.title: Brothel In Belize: Machine Machine Fall 2026
events.note: A one-night label showcase under its own name. Doors seven, $41.

events.title: Cannelle with Baldgirl
events.note: French-American folk sung mostly in French, fingerpicked and very quiet. $18–22.

events.title: Internet Girl with OSHE
events.note: Hyperpop built from blown-out guitars and a laptop. Doors seven, all ages.

events.title: DJ Stingray: Throttle Techno
events.note: Sherard Ingram in the balaclava, playing electro at the speed Drexciya meant it. One of the best DJ bookings of the month; 1015 lists no set time.

events.title: After Dark Industrial Dance Party
events.note: EBM, industrial and coldwave on the Knockout's floor. Off the DICE calendar.

events.title: Perennial Beats Happy Hour
events.note: Records from six, no cover, before the industrial night takes the room.

events.title: Two Runner with Dessert Boys
events.note: A fiddle-and-banjo duo out of the Sierra foothills who play old-time music without the costume. Off the DICE calendar.

events.title: DJ Maryzelle
events.note: Late set after the Two Runner show, off the DICE calendar.

events.title: Computerwife with Double Helix Peace Treaty
events.note: Bedroom-made guitar pop in a converted Richmond cinema. Songkick carries the music; the repertory film side of the room is not readable.

events.title: Stanley Kubrick's The Killing (4K restoration)
events.note: Kubrick's 1956 racetrack heist, the first film where the structure is the point. Restored, and short enough to make a double bill of the evening.

events.title: Wild at Heart (4K restoration) — costume night
events.note: Lynch's Palme d'Or winner with free popcorn for anyone in costume. The listing still refers to Halloween, three weeks after it.

events.title: Love Birds, with Judy Irving in person
events.note: A screening with a post-film conversation moderated by Irving, who made The Wild Parrots of Telegraph Hill.

events.title: NightLife: You, Your Friends and 60,000 Creatures
events.note: The Academy's 21+ Thursday — the aquarium, the rainforest and the planetarium after dark with a bar in them. Six till ten, last entry nine, $26.

events.title: Waterfront Walkabout: The Holiday Season Finale
events.note: The last Big Art Loop stroll of the year, Pier 14 to the Exploratorium, five till eight. Free; RSVP for the guided version.

events.title: Micro to Macro: Microorganisms, Sound and Robots
events.note: Scott Kildall and Kal Spelletich on building machines that listen to bacteria. Gray Area publishes no time.

events.title: Transcendence: Free Choral Music and Poetry Readings
events.note: Choral music interleaved with poetry, free with a suggested donation. Funcheap names no room, so the venue is unconfirmed.

events.title: 16th and Mission Open Mic
events.note: No stage, no microphone, no bookers. It has been running on that plaza for years and is the most purely public performance in the city.

events.title: Salt & Spirit: An Operatic Experience Rooted in Gullah-Geechee Spirituals
events.note: Opera Parallèle's world premiere, built on Gullah-Geechee spirituals, on the Steindler Stage. Second of three remaining performances after last week's opening; the other is Saturday.

events.title: GWAR with Midnight, Nailed Shut and Mac Sabbath
events.note: Forty years of latex and fake blood, with Cleveland's Midnight and a McDonald's-themed Sabbath tribute beneath them. Sold out. Doors six, show 7:45, $45.

events.title: Pretty Lights
events.note: First of three nights of Derek Vincent Smith's sample-built electro-soul, now with a live band. Doors 6:30. BART — the garage gates shut at seven.

events.title: KATSEYE
events.note: The globally assembled girl group's arena run. Deprioritised by the brief and findable without it; listed for completeness.

events.title: As I Lay Dying
events.note: The Berkeley date, a night after Santa Cruz. Cornerstone's calendar did not load; found on the sweep.

events.title: Brian Culbertson
events.note: Third and last of the sold-out run. $89–139.

events.title: Corey Harris with Cedric Watson
events.note: Delta blues guitar and Creole fiddle on one bill — Harris plays the pre-war repertoire straight, Watson sings in Louisiana French.

events.title: El Tee with Maiden Mare and Hallie Austin
events.note: Three songwriters on an Albany bill. Through JamBase, which gives no time.

events.title: Cycotic Youth, Terminally Ill and more
events.note: Five dollars, all ages, volunteer-run, as it has been since 1986.

events.title: La Chinoise
events.note: Godard's 1967 film about students playing at Maoism, which is funnier and crueller than its reputation.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: Temescal's Thursday room, free with an RSVP.

events.title: The Who's Tommy
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Third of six performances.

events.title: Gianmarco Soresi
events.note: Second night of the run; late show 9:45.

events.title: Corey O'Brien
events.note: A night of the Sunnyvale club's own booking. $40.

events.title: World Ballet Company: Swan Lake
events.note: A touring Swan Lake. The Heritage publishes no time and its own events page shows nothing this week; from the resale feed.

events.title: Free Grant Yun Interactive 3D Landscape Art Experience
events.note: A free walk-in installation of the painter's flat-plane landscapes rebuilt in three dimensions, noon till ten.

events.title: Filoli Unwrapped
events.note: The second of three this week.

events.title: Michael Nau
events.note: Session Room date, a night after Santa Cruz. Does not clear the drive; recorded rather than recommended.

events.title: Rosebud and Shaky Feelin'
events.note: Local reggae-rock double bill in the redwoods. Below the outer bar.

events.title: The Mountain Goats — Night Five: Cast of Thousands
events.note: Night five goes back to 2002's Cast of Thousands, the record that marked the end of the boombox years. No door time published.

events.title: The Complete Philip Glass Piano Etudes
events.note: All twenty etudes in one sitting, divided among ten pianists — Timo Andres, Aaron Diehl, Daniela Liebman and Jason Moran among them. Glass is not attending. The most ambitious single programme of the week and it only happens once.

events.title: HUG: Gyan Riley, Devendra Banhart, Noah Georgeson
events.note: Three players who have orbited each other for twenty years — Riley's classical guitar, Banhart's voice, Georgeson's production — in a room with red velvet and a chandelier. Doors seven.

events.title: Carl Cox with Seth Troxler
events.note: Two generations of techno in a warehouse on the waterfront. Found on the sweep; no set times published, and a pier is not a venue with a calendar.

events.title: Earthless with Terry Gross and Carlton Melton
events.note: San Diego instrumental psych that treats a riff as a twenty-minute proposition, on a bill with two Bay Area bands of the same mind. Sold out. Doors 7:30, $25 advance.

events.title: Eivør with midori jaeger
events.note: Faroese singer whose records sit between folk ballad and electronic drone; the voice carries most of it unaccompanied.

events.title: Maddie Zahm: Everything All The Time, with OSTON
events.note: Confessional pop about leaving evangelical Idaho. Doors eight, $28–33.

events.title: Natural Child with Buzzed Lightbeer, Milk for the Angry, Catnip
events.note: Nashville boogie-rock, loose on purpose, with three local bands under them. Doors eight, $25–30.

events.title: Anthony Jeselnik
events.note: Two nights of the most precisely written mean jokes in American stand-up. No support.

events.title: DANNA: The Bedroom Sessions
events.note: Danna Paola, the Mexican pop star, in a 1,400-seat cinema rather than an arena — the stripped-back version of the show.

events.title: Layton Giordani
events.note: New York techno, built for big rooms. The Regency publishes no times.

events.title: James Hype with Hans Glader
events.note: Technical, tightly mixed house for a very large room. Through Songkick; The Midway lists no set times.

events.title: Hiroko Yamamura and FJAAK
events.note: Chicago techno and Berlin hardware live. Public Works' own site sat behind a verification wall this run; from the sweep.

events.title: Westend with TOBEHONEST
events.note: Tech-house on the main floor. No set time published.

events.title: Cool Customer and Chris Karns
events.note: Doors ten, 21+. Karns is a turntablist with a DMC title behind him.

events.title: Paul Collins: The Best of The Nerves, The Beat and The Exploding Hearts — Night 1
events.note: Collins wrote Hanging on the Telephone before Blondie recorded it, and this is two nights of that songbook in a 150-cap bar. Off the DICE calendar.

events.title: Bop Nite DJs
events.note: Sold out. The late room after the Paul Collins set.

events.title: Love T.K.O. Disco Dance Party
events.note: Seventies disco and sweet soul on 45s. Off the DICE calendar, which carries this night twice; it is one party.

events.title: Black Vinyl Happy Hour
events.note: Records from five, no cover.

events.title: Babehoven
events.note: Maya Bon's slow, close-miked songs in the Richmond cinema. Songkick gives no time.

events.title: Zhang Yimou's Raise the Red Lantern (4K restoration)
events.note: The 1991 film restored, co-presented with the Bay Area Chinese Culture Salon. Gong Li in the role that made her.

events.title: New People: Soul Patrol, with J.M. Harper in person
events.note: The director in the room afterwards. Japantown, 1746 Post Street.

events.title: New People: In the Mood for Love
events.note: Wong Kar-wai's 2000 film in the Japantown cinema — the right size of screen for it.

events.title: Aliens (Special Edition)
events.note: The long cut, with the sentry guns back in.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics' Presents
events.note: Six till eight at 57 Post Street, in the 1854 library's own room. $5 members, $10 otherwise; the title is not published in advance on the readable listing.

events.title: ODC Presents: Global Dance Passport Fall 2026
events.note: ODC's survey of resident and visiting companies — the Mission's dance house doing what it is for. Three performances across Friday and Saturday.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The last free hour of the week, nine to ten.

events.title: From the E: Harvest Night Market
events.note: An Outer Mission street market with food stalls and makers, free with an RSVP — the sort of neighbourhood programming that never reaches a ticketing platform.

events.title: Film: Defiant to the Last — the Tule Lake Jail
events.note: A free documentary on the stockade at the Tule Lake incarceration camp. Funcheap names no room, so the venue is unconfirmed.

events.title: John Waters Cult Cinema Night: Cry-Baby and Serial Mom
events.note: A double bill of Waters's two most watchable studio pictures. $15–25; the listing names no cinema.

events.title: Trash Prom Walk of Shame: Runway as Performance Art
events.note: Wearable sculpture made from refuse, walked down a runway in a design showroom. $25.

events.title: Lofi Lounge Vinyl DJ Pop Up
events.note: Seven till ten, records in a downtown izakaya. Free.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, the order set by the audience shouting numbers. Running weekly; $13 at the door, $16 online.

events.title: Pretty Lights
events.note: Second of three nights. Doors 6:30; take BART.

events.title: Gerald Albright
events.note: Two nights of the saxophonist's funk-leaning jazz. $38–89.

events.title: Haley Heynderickx with Greg Mendez
events.note: Portland fingerstyle songs that take sudden loud turns, with Philadelphia's Greg Mendez, who writes the quietest devastating verses going. The best folk bill of the week.

events.title: MDC with Damage Party and Fast Friends
events.note: Millions of Dead Cops, forty-plus years on, the night before they co-headline Potrero. Through JamBase; no time.

events.title: Dev Lemons
events.note: Pop songwriting explained and then performed. Cornerstone's calendar did not load; from the sweep.

events.title: Bad Camper, Dark Satellite, The Morning Drive
events.note: Five dollars, all ages.

events.title: Harakiri
events.note: Kobayashi's 1962 film, the one that takes the samurai code apart from the inside. Four in the afternoon.

events.title: CineSpin: He Who Gets Slapped
events.note: The 1924 Chaney silent with a live score — BAMPFA's CineSpin series, which is the best reason to be in Berkeley on a Friday night.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy Show
events.note: Address sent on RSVP, free with the code. Standing Friday night.

events.title: Free All-BIPOC Drag King Show with Dark Electronic DJs
events.note: A drag king bill with industrial DJs after, sliding scale $5–15 and free for Black queer and trans attendees.

events.title: The Who's Tommy
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Fourth of six performances.

events.title: Opera San José: Fiddler on the Roof
events.note: Opera San José staging Bock and Harnick with opera voices and an orchestra in the pit, which changes the show. In a run to 29 November.

events.title: Shoreline Mafia: Who Want The Smoke 2026
events.note: A West Coast rap package — SOB x RBE, Mike Sherm, 03 Greedo, Kamaiyah and more beneath Shoreline Mafia. An arena bill, but an unusually deep one.

events.title: Mike Sherm
events.note: An afterparty set the same night he plays the SAP Center package. Ten o'clock, 21+.

events.title: Gianmarco Soresi
events.note: Third night; late show 9:45.

events.title: Ryan Goodcase
events.note: Two nights at the Sunnyvale club. $39.

events.title: Harriet: Trying to Get the Feeling Again
